terms.gloss: organise, get up (a dinner, a wedding, games)
evidence: Ter. Ad. 966: apparāre dē diē convīvium
Cic. Q. fr. 3.8 (Lewis & Short): lūdōs magnificentissimōs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: to prepare “esp. with effort, care, expense”; its noun apparātus is the preparations (see prepare).

terms.gloss: lay on, set up (a meal, a feast)
evidence: Liv. 3.29.5: epulae īnstrūctae dīcuntur fuisse ante omnium domūs

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with an accusative and a gerundive
evidence: Caes. BG 1.13 (Lewis & Short): pontem in Ararī faciundum
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to cause something to be done … (in good prose and very freq.; predominant in Cæsar)”: cēnam parandam cūrāre, to see that dinner is made.

phrases.latin: Occīdunt mē quidem dum nimis sānctās nūptiās student facere: in apparandō cōnsūmunt diem.
phrases.english: They’re killing me, wanting to make the wedding too perfect: they’re spending the whole day on the arrangements.

phrases.latin: sī bellī homunculī conlēctī sunt, sī ēlēctus locus, sī tempus lēctum, sī apparātus nōn neglēctus
phrases.english: if nice people have been brought together, if the place has been chosen, the time picked, and the preparations not neglected

sources: Lewis & Short: apparo · Lewis & Short: instruo · Lewis & Short: curo
